<reason>Side A won decisively by engaging both halves of the motion ("local residents or members") and ruthlessly exposing two fatal contradictions in Side B's case. First, after Side B argued in its opening that dynamic pricing helps budget-conscious locals find fifty-dollar bargains, Side B argued in Rebuttal 1 that the general sale is "a bloodbath of bots and speed" where spiking prices lock buyers out. Side A pressed this contradiction in Pressure Questions and forced Side B to explicitly concede in Rebuttal 2 that dynamic markets "fail locals during sell-out surges." Second, Side A showed that Side B's proposed alternative of means-tested discounts required far more invasive paperwork (tax or benefits data) than billing postal codes while relying on the exact same non-transferability mechanisms Side B claimed scalpers would bypass. Side A also cleanly answered Side B's concern about sick locals via closed face-value return exchanges and protected loyal traveling fans via the member reserve, whereas Side B had its opening clipped and repeated refuted points in closing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's weaponization of Side B's "bloodbath of bots and speed" admission [B2.5] against Side B's earlier claim that dynamic pricing helps locals find bargains [B1.6], combined with Side A's expose of the double standard in Side B's means-tested discount counterplan [A2.1, A4.4, A5.2].</best_rebuttal>
